newsitem.title: FRANCE: SAA to add ex-Paris cargo capacity in July.
newsitem.headline: SAA to add ex-Paris cargo capacity in July.

text.p: South African Airways said cargo capacity from Paris to Johannesburg will be be increased from July 1 when it adds a fourth Boeing 747 passenger flight.
"Three of these frequencies will be operated by an 747SP and the remaining one by a 747-300," an SAA official told Reuters.
SAA now operates three 747 SPs on the route offering four pallet capacity per flight, the equivalent of approximately seven tonnes.
Cargo capacity is shared with SAA's Zurich station as the flight is routed via Zurich to Johannesburg.
"The 747-300 offers double the cargo capacity of an SP so it's good news given that load factors for freight are good on the route and the market outlook is very positive," the official said.
Despite favourable market conditions, there was limited scope to increase rates because of fluid capacity on the route from Europe.

"Frankly, we would risk pricing ourselves out of our prime market if we increased rates as there is no shortage of "indirect" carriers on the route who resort to discounting. At the same time, the fact that we have a significant market share should mean we are setting the pace."
"But until we begin developing onward destinations from Johannesburg, to other areas in southern Africa, we are obliged to adopt a prudent policy on rates."

SAA's Paris cargo station is also allocated capacity on the South African airline's scheduled full-freighter services from Frankfurt and Amsterdam to Johannesburg. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax 5017
